study.question: Can unit-mass history tokens support shared field/task interaction while a separate exposure-amplified direct path preserves click discrimination? Observations: mass_sum and count_scaled nearly tied (0.654943/0.654925 click AUC), ahead of mass_normalized (0.644929). At equal 403,396 dense parameters, scaled_pair (0.656159) beat split (0.653866), normalized_pair (0.639232) and fused_pair (0.653906), so neither an extra bank nor early scale averaging sufficed. The latest task_scale kept shared transport scaled and changed only auxiliary direct readout: click moved 0.656159 -> 0.656226, but cart fell 0.846545 -> 0.828608, fav fell 0.870637 -> 0.870328 and buy rose 0.868736 -> 0.881166. Cart recovery and the unexplored shared-transport factor are consequential uncertainties; the tiny click difference is not established beyond this seed.
study.hypothesis: Separating content scale by computational path, rather than putting both scales in a common token bank, may let shared interaction retain semantic content while the click tower still sees history magnitude. The proposed candidate routes unit-mass summaries into shared attention, amplified summaries into the click direct skip, and unit-mass summaries into auxiliary skips. Existing shared attention was always amplified in the latest readout study, so normalization of its contents has not been isolated with the click direct path retained. Predict recovery of cart ranking without loss of click ranking; this is a provisional path-routing hypothesis, not evidence of negative transfer or gradient conflict.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text, lines 271-277, already motivates unnormalized activation intensity. We inherit the concern about magnitude, not novelty of interest intensity. Our sigmoid-normalized field summaries use deterministic n/2 scaling and factor its placement between shared interaction and direct task skips; this is not an exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark source 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d, lines 113-239, verifies target pooling, field/task tokenization, residual interaction and task-token readout. We retain the local parent ordinary fieldwise-QKV stack and direct paths; the intervention is pre-projection history scale in shared tokens independently of direct readout. Original HiFormer full paper is not audited; no priority claim.

Pinned benchmark source lines 123-219 uses task-mask-pooled sequence hubs and layer-wise aggregation/broadcast. We add no hubs, gates or per-task retrieval; fixed shared transport and direct skips receive different deterministic content scales. Original paper:infnet is link-only in the registry, so originality relative to it remains unresolved.

Archived section 2.3 describes nearby stacked and layer-wise families. It supplies taxonomy, not evidence that path-scale separation works and not a complete original-method audit. This is a controlled local representation study; algorithmic novelty remains unverified.

inherited_components: Entire g0-r0003-task_scale model architecture, authorized inputs, embeddings, field queries/keys, global history retrieval, overlapping feedback presence/counts, projection banks, static skips, interaction blocks and task towers
Both deterministic history views already computed by the parent, with absence gating and projection/count/bias arithmetic retained

study.proposed_difference: Add only transport_scale, a parameter-free selector before token concatenation: scaled selects projected summaries based on n/2 times normalized pooled contents; normalized selects projections of the same unit-mass contents. Counts, projection biases, absence gates and token identities are never divided by n. Compute both projections in all arms. Orthogonally cross the existing auxiliary_readout_scale while keeping click_readout_scale=scaled. T=scaled/A=normalized reproduces task_scale and T=scaled/A=scaled reproduces scaled_reference. No extra layers, tokens, parameters, fields, losses or training changes.
predictions: Define Y(T,A) for each task metric, T in {scaled,normalized} shared transport and A in {scaled,normalized} auxiliary direct readout. Compare Y(normalized,A)-Y(scaled,A) at each A and the interaction [Y(normalized,normalized)-Y(scaled,normalized)]-[Y(normalized,scaled)-Y(scaled,scaled)]. Report all cells and contrasts for click AUC/Logloss and each auxiliary separately.

If the proposed path separation is useful, transport_norm_aux_norm improves cart AUC relative to transport_scaled_aux_norm while preserving or improving primary click AUC. Shared transport effects in both A settings support a transport contribution; an effect only with normalized A suggests interaction rather than a universal normalization benefit.

Capacity is identical, with expected 32,196,612 total parameters; both views are already computed in the parent, so major cost growth is not expected. Report measured allocated GPU/wall time, train time, examples, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95 latency; equal epochs alone do not establish equal compute.

Primary selection remains highest full-validation click AUC. Auxiliary metrics diagnose the hypothesis and cannot replace that selection rule. Retain baseline-din, prior alternatives and both replays in performance tables. Single-seed wins are preliminary.

Use pre-existing history bins empty, 1-16, 17-64, >64 with sample/positive/negative counts; negative counts are samples minus positives. Slice differences are exploratory; the prior long-history reversal motivates inspection, not a guarantee. Request other authorized composition/frequency/hour/missing-field slices only if host exposes them; do not invent unavailable timestamps or user IDs.

With common fixed weights and buffers in eval mode, all arms agree when exposure count is 0 or 2; n/2 is then either applied to zero pooled contents or equals one. Scaled-transport controls must reproduce their respective parents before interpreting trained results.
falsifiers: No cart recovery and lower click AUC for normalized transport in both auxiliary settings contradict the proposed useful transport/direct separation in this architecture and recipe; retain the better existing reference.

If only the auxiliary-readout factor explains changes and both matched transport effects are null, there is no support for shared content normalization as the mechanism. Null interaction refutes any claim that the factors require coordination, not necessarily their main effects.

If auxiliary recovery occurs only at a click cost, record the tradeoff and reject a joint-quality improvement claim. If a click gain occurs without cart recovery, it can still select a candidate provisionally but does not support the cart-recovery explanation.

Parameter-count mismatch, changed masks/inputs/training, nonfinite tensors, failed padding invariance, or failed parent replay invalidates attribution. Execution failure is not scientific counterevidence. One unsuccessful seed does not refute all path-conditioned representations.
alternative_explanations: All observed differences may reflect seed variation or single-pass convergence rather than a durable representation advantage. The +0.000067 click AUC is especially weak evidence.

LayerNorm does not remove the intervention: scaling content before adding bias/count/identity changes relative directions and gradients. Learned projections, Dice batch statistics and shared embeddings could explain performance changes; this factorial does not separate them.

Earlier field_feedback lost to field_global (0.640614 vs 0.646474), and split/fused banks failed to beat scaled_pair. These negative trajectories argue against simply adding feedback groups or both scales, but do not globally refute those architectures; we keep retrieval/grouping fixed here.

Whole-window vocabularies/static snapshots and official_offline delayed-feedback visibility limit interpretation. Auxiliary labels concern user/category/brand actions within 24 hours, not advertisement-level conversion. No production point-in-time or outside-benchmark transfer claim.

Industry usage records show consideration, not adoption of hubs, reversible mixing, sparse filters or repeated retrieval. Prior methods are external references with no local efficacy established. No personal source or populated scoped memory was available; agent searches returned no matches.
